Order filled. Here's my summary.

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy within my mandate. Apple remains a highly profitable, cash-generative business: fiscal 2024 revenue was **$391.0 billion** (up 2% from $383.3 billion), **net income was $93.7 billion** (I cite the exact reported figure of $93,736 million), and operating cash flow was **$118.3 billion**. Net income was modestly below FY2023's $97.0 billion, but that decline is fully attributable to a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid decision — operating income actually increased to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion, and Services revenue grew 13%, so the underlying business is strengthening rather than deteriorating. With the quote at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and $50,000 in cash with no prior purchases today, I placed a single buy limit order for **44 shares of AAPL at a limit price of $222.75**, which filled at $222.75 for a total of about **$9,801** — within the $10,000 per-order cap, under the $20,000 daily total, at a price essentially at market, buy-only, with no money leaving the account. I relied on the FY2024 net income, revenue, and operating cash flow figures cited above.
